attack_surfaces.operation: WRITE to msg[idx] heap buffer via read(0, msg[idx], msg_size[idx]-1)
attack_surfaces.reason: attacker-controlled index reaches pointer dereference (msg[idx]) and write destination; index check is idx < cookie_num with no explicit lower-bound — if idx can be made to select an out-of-bounds slot or a freed/reused slot, write goes to attacker-chosen heap pointer. msg_size[idx]-1 controls write length.

attack_surfaces.operation: FREE msg[idx], then msg[idx] = msg[cookie_num-1]; msg_size[idx] = msg_size[cookie_num-1]; cookie_num--
attack_surfaces.reason: free-then-reuse pattern: when idx == cookie_num-1, the freed pointer is written back into the same msg slot (msg[idx] = msg[cookie_num-1] where idx==cookie_num-1), leaving a dangling pointer in msg[idx] that is still reachable via edit_cookie/read_cookie. Classic UAF/double-free surface for S2.

attack_surfaces.operation: calloc(size,1); read(0, buf, size); msg[cookie_num]=buf; msg_size[cookie_num]=size
attack_surfaces.reason: user-controlled allocation size (<=0x100) and message content; size stored as int in msg_size array. calloc zeroes buffer. New entry appended at cookie_num index.

attack_surfaces.operation: READ heap content printed to stdout
attack_surfaces.reason: heap content printed before free — if heap contains pointers/libc addresses (e.g. from prior frees into unsorted bin), this leaks them. Index is random though, not directly attacker-controlled.
